key_insight: An evidence-aware AI framework integrates diverse pharmacovigilance sources into a knowledge resource that improved downstream adverse drug event (ADE) synthesis and extraction.
clinical_relevance: The resource could support drug-safety research by making ADE evidence, provenance, and confidence more accessible, but clinical benefit was not established.
method: Integrate FAERS reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and Mass General Brigham electronic health records.
Combine LLM extraction, ontology-based normalization, and cross-source evidence assessment.
Prioritize relationships using statistical and machine learning methods and infer ADE links through drug ingredients.
evidence_signal: The resource contains over 2.47 million relationships; evaluations reported better LLM ADE synthesis quality and higher clinical ADE extraction precision and F1, without numerical gains in the abstract.
watch_item: Confidence-scored drug–ADE links should not be treated as causal findings; the abstract does not establish prospective clinical safety or effectiveness.
paper_title: AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance
